utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You were defending part of the United Kingdom against aggression by various paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: These groups committed atrocities against the civilian population, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And against police officers.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And despite the best effort of you and your troops, that happened while you were in that theatre.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And I'm sure that made you feel angry, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall if anger was the response, but it would have disturbed me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Disturbed.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Concerned me greatly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, really it would be less than human not to be disturbed, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Yes. And on other occasions also, you were aware that Mr. Stojic expressed strong views about what he saw as wrongdoing on the part of certain Muslim elements.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And because you were there as a monitor, there would be nothing untoward about Mr. Stojic expressing that opinion to you. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And now because this has been dealt with by other counsel, I think I can come to it quite briefly. I think we've established over the last few hours of cross-examination that there were occasions when Muslim elements did commit atrocities against others.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: And with the limited staff that you had, it wasn't possible nor was it your function for you to investigate each of those things in detail.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have done our best to confirm whether or not they had taken place and some responsibility, yes, but it was not possible to permanently investigate; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Right. So you would gather information as best you could.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: But clearly there was a lot that you were not able to investigate yourself.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Nor were your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: I think, also, you testified that there were certain -- I think the phrase that was used were "uncontrolled elements" of the HVO operating.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: You gave evidence that it was not always easy to identify who they were because their uniforms might not be in the best condition.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: So we can accept that they also may have been involved in certain illegal activities, can't we?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may we go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Beese --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in open session. Counsel Nozica, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. I'm trying to use every bit of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My name is Senka Nozica. I'm going to ask you questions on behalf of the Defence counsel of Bruno Stojic. My colleague indicated or, rather, spoke about your report of the 20th of April, 1993. It is a report which has a Prosecution number. It is 01981. So while I'm asking the questions, might we have that document placed on our screens. It is a report that you talked about, and you said that Mr. Stojic, although you did see it, entered an attacked Mr. Ganic over alleged information about matters that took place on the ground. Is this the report? The date is the 21st of April. Just let me check that. Because in translation it says the 20th of April. But, yes, it's the 21st of April, 1993. That's it. You've just said that things did happen in theatre, that you investigated certain things, others not. Now, I'd like to indicate two points on page 2 that I consider to be important. It's on the next page. And it is at the bottom of page 2. That's the portion that I'd like to base my question on. And it's the first portion. It says: "The regional centre of Zenica is attempting to negotiate a local cease-fire agreement since early on the 18th of April, 1993. Consecutive meetings with local authorities took place in the municipality but first without result due to the absence of a military commander from the HVO side." Do you remember that report and that section where mention is made of the military commander of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I've seen this report, but I understand the context.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If you don't remember the report, then take a look at the next paragraph, the last sentence there, because it refers to what you said about the interrupted meeting.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The initial meeting, et cetera. So that report addresses both those events. I'm now going to ask you or, rather, show you some documents which relate to Mr. Stojic's reactions, and then we'll go back to the matter of the absence of the HVO commander at the meeting. I'll probably do that tomorrow morning in the time I have. We're now going to look at a series of documents which will show us what information Mr. Stojic had on that day about the situation on the ground, and my question later on will be whether you know anything about those events and whether you took note of them and what your conclusions were and whether you consider that those events or, rather, the information that Mr. Stojic received were of such a character that they could cause him disquiet or anger. We're not all the same. We're different personalities. You quite obviously are a rational person. You probably find -- you're probably not angry very often, but other people might be. Am I right when I make that observation? Well, can we take a look --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not an easy one to answer, I'm afraid. I would hope to be able to remain calm even if I was disturbed. I am sometimes angry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. But nonetheless, in your -- in one's evaluation, one cannot always stem from oneself, especially when assessing other people. Then in addition to what we observe about them, we try to -- we have to understand that we're not all the same. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: May we now take a look at Defence Exhibit 2D 00099. I'm going to try and save time. It's a short document. I'll tell you what it's about straight away. This is a document of the Croatian Defence Council. We haven't got it on our screens yet. The command of the Central Bosnia operative zone, the department for information. The date is the 16th of April, 1993. And it's called "Statement For The Public". Any problems with the document? No. We have it on the ELMO. Thank you. We can read it out. It's a public announcement. "After a series of terrorist actions in the area of Central Bosnia, on April the 16th at 5.45 hours, Muslim forces committed a brutal attack on the command of the operational sector of Central Bosnia with the aim of destroying the command. "The Croatian defence council returned the aggressors' fire." The next document will be 2D 00097, please. I'm going to show you this whole set of documents, and then I'll come back to my initial questions, once again to try and save time. It is the same operative zone, Central Bosnia. The report is an extraordinary report dated the 18th of April, 1993. It is one page long, signed by Mr. Tihomir Blaskic, and it says: "Extreme Muslim forces are continuing their attack, the aim of which is to break down the HVO completely and to expel the Croatian people from the Lasva River valley and to cut off complete communication between Konjic, Jablanica, and Gornji Vakuf." I don't want to read it all. I'm sure the Trial Chamber will look at all the reports carefully. I just want to show you the events in sequence and the information that Mr. Stojic had. Just let us establish whether -- rather, what information he received. The next document is document 2D 00100. Once again, the Croatian Defence Council. We're just waiting for the document to appear on our screens. The commander of the Central Bosnian events in Vitez. Once again it is the 18th of April, 1993, and it says: "At approximately 2400 hours on the 17th of April, 1993, the Muslim Mujahedin forces are continuing their ceaseless aggression in Central Bosnia with a dominant attack on Busovaca, Vitez, and the Croatian territory of Zenica, and in other areas are launching serious preparations to go into action." Have you had a chance to look at those documents, that particular one?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would now like to show you two important documents. One has already been tendered. The number is 2D 00021.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry, I would like to make an intermediary footnote observation. We much appreciate Defence teams letting us have the documents they present, and some teams present them in a way that you have a file, and they name a document and you find it. But others, and there were two examples this time and this is one, you have a file where the documents are in an order which does not merit that time -- that title, if you allow. It is impossible to find the document because they are all up and down, the figures, and then it is of no use at all because, as we do not want to -- to slow down, things pass and we look at the ELMO and here and there. So in the future, it would be very helpful if that could be improved. We appreciate the effort. We know it's a lot of the work, but it is -- the work is more or less wasted if there is no order that helps us find the documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was certain that we had organised them in the order in which I'm calling them out. It's just that I'm trying to save time. Well, those four documents are classed together, but the problem is time. If I had enough time, I would wait for the document to appear on e-court, on our screens, and then there would be no problem. But I'll slow down a little bit. I have five more minutes, and then I would complete this showing of documents. So 2D 00021 is that document. We have that in front of us, and it is an order, and we can see what it's about. It says: "The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 1st Mostar Brigade." That is a document of the 19th of April, and you can take a look at the last page of the document and you'll be able to see that it is an order in fact from Mr. Hujdur, the commander of the 41st Motorised Brigade. We can go back to the first page now, please, and then we'll see that this document is called "Order." "Order for Defence," as my colleague showed a similar order yesterday. However, the order for defence, this one has an addition, and I'd like us to take a look at that. The addition to the order for defence, and that is 2D 00095, that is the document's number. It has an annex. 2D 000 -- yes. This is interesting. This is an "Order For Defence," as it's called, and that is the additional portion, and it should be a list of signals to be used or, in other words, they are signals, different coloured signals, ribbons or bands, that are used in attacking or defending. So along with the Order For Defence, it is interesting to take a look at the central portion. Thank you. It says here: "The Command of the 41st Motorised Brigade." The date is the same, the 19th of April, and it says: "With the RAK-625 signal, begin with an all-out attack at all places along the axes already set." We have three types like this, but it is obvious that this order was an order for attack and not an order for defence. Now, my question is as follows: Having seen these documents and the information, we're mostly speaking about information because this order was issued the following day on the 19th of April, and if we look at all the previous information that Mr. Stojic had, do you know that these events actually took place? Did you investigate them? And do you think that it was sufficient reason for the person receiving this kind of information to be alarmed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTOPHER BEESE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on the final document you've shown, but the earlier ones mentioning aggression, particularly in Central Bosnia, are interesting, particularly when much of the activity and action taken by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was directly in response to military attack by the HVO. For the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to react when pressed is hardly surprising. And therefore, to say that it is aggression as if it was blatant and initial aggression is misleading, and I would say that the first few documents we saw were part of a propaganda exercise. I cannot comment on the last one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The last document shows precisely that that was not propaganda, Mr. Beese, and it seems of that very clearly. But I think that His Honour is going to interrupt me, so thank you, and I'll continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is five minutes past 7.00. We'll close for the day and reconvene tomorrow at 2.15.
